original_test_intent: Validate the BMC Resource Management power information and temporary CPU/system power cap under CPU stress, then restore the documented default.
original_method: Resolve the exact BMC chassis resource and whether its cap represents CPU package, node or chassis input power; snapshot all corresponding limits and telemetry; apply one approved cap and read it back; run a bounded CPU workload sufficient to request above-cap power while sampling the authoritative measurement domain and thermals; judge limiting with an approved tolerance; stop stress, Restore Default and prove baseline health and limits are restored.
manual_activity: The platform owner defines the resource and power domain, cap/default values, CPU stress and abort envelope; an operator authorizes writes/stress, observes recovery and confirms final restoration.
required_inputs: Supported BMC Resource Power/PowerControl write schema
Definition of cap domain: CPU package, node or chassis
Authoritative matching power telemetry and units
Bounded CPU workload, duration and affinity
Sampling interval, enforcement tolerance and demand sufficiency
safety_requirements: Do not guess the chassis resource or power domain
Do not cap or stress a host with active unapproved workloads
Validate the cap range and units before writing
Read back the selected resource before stress
Monitor thermals, machine checks, throttling and BMC health
Stop on over-limit, alarm, sensor loss or instability
Never automatically retry write, stress or restore
Verify default restoration with matching-domain telemetry
Preserve logs and do not clear evidence
agent_execution_scope: Resolve and capture resource/CPU power baseline
Apply one approved cap and read it back
Run only the approved bounded CPU workload
Sample complete BMC/IPMI/Redfish and OS power/thermal data
Verify baseline/default health and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve cap/default value, workload, tolerance and abort rules

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Filtered sensors and a chassis name list are preliminary discovery only; they do not select or read the PowerControl resource, perform any cap/stress/restore step or protect credentials/TLS.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the documented BMC Resource Power control for the mapped domain, write/read one approved cap, execute bounded CPU stress while collecting matching-domain time-series power and thermals, then Restore Default and prove readback/baseline.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Resource management Power, CPU stress, Restore Default and 10/10-minute estimates are retained; cap value, domain and workload are owner inputs.

modernized_recommendation.status: MAPPED CPU OR SYSTEM POWER-CAP ENFORCEMENT TRANSACTION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a resource ledger containing chassis URI, control scope, original/default cap, requested/read-back cap, CPU topology/workload, matched power sensors, time-series maximum/tolerance, restore response and final health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the missing control-to-measurement mapping, sufficiency oracle, abort monitoring and restoration proof without changing the source workflow.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A GPU cap result cannot cover CPU/system power; an IPMI power grep or chassis list cannot cover control writes or enforcement.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: CPU-package watts and AC/chassis input watts differ by platform losses and other loads; comparing the wrong domains can falsely pass or fail a correctly enforced cap.

project_override_considerations: The Project must explicitly define what BMC `Resource management - Power` controls and which watts the criterion means. This is an execution mapping input; if vendor documentation cannot establish it, execution must stop rather than invent a conversion.
expected_evidence: Verified SUT/BMC/chassis/CPU identity and documented control-to-measurement domain map
Original/default/cap matrix, CPU stress/tolerance/abort plan and approvals
Complete BMC/IPMI/Redfish and OS power/thermal baseline
Protected cap write/readback tied to the exact resource
CPU workload transcript, demand sufficiency and synchronized power/thermal time series
Restore Default readback, baseline health, MCE/kernel/SEL events, recovery/no-secret audit and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently require power information, cap application, CPU stress enforcement and restoration. The exact resource-to-CPU measurement mapping is unspecified but can be supplied by normal platform documentation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The supported resource schema, cap domain, workload and tolerance are normal project/vendor inputs; review does not guess them and the intended lifecycle remains clear.

review_improvement: Restores all mutating and stress checkpoints and prevents an invalid comparison between an unidentified chassis control and unrelated CPU power telemetry.
independent_technical_reasoning: Cap enforcement is meaningful only when the control scope and measured watts describe the same power boundary. CPU package telemetry excludes memory, conversion losses and other board loads, while chassis input includes them. The reviewer must therefore require an explicit domain map, adequate workload demand and time-series tolerance before calling the BMC cap effective.
